_comment: ZKETech EB Tester device table — extracted from eb.exe v1.8.9 binary at offsets 0x1E634 (main) and 0x1F64C (extended). See protocol.md for full documentation.

deviceIdByte._comment: Mapping from RX frame byte 16 (the 'device ID byte', aka the old 'device constant') to the device name displayed by the EB Tester. Established via fake-device probing Apr 2026. Reference device is EBC-A40L (byte 16 = 0x0A). The probe sweep 0x00..0xEF was run 2026-04-22 and 42 distinct devices were mapped across 0x01..0x2A; see scripts/probes/2026-04-22_00-44-35-byte16/device-names.curated.json for the full audit trail (OCR confidence, mirror cross-checks, visual verifications).
_notes: CONFIRMED mirror pattern: byte16 N in 0x01..0x2A produces the same device name as N+0x64 (in 0x65..0x8E). All 42 primary-range readings were cross-validated against their mirrors where both were clean.
Range 0x2B..0x64 (58 values) all display 'No Device' — this is the gap between the primary byte16 range and the mirror range.

Range 0x8F..0xEF (97 values) all display 'No Device' — confirmed by direct OCR of row 1 in every probe. This is the second rejected range. Provenance: 0x8F..0xB8 from the original 2026-04-22 sweep; 0xB9..0xDC from the 2026-04-22T18:00Z re-sweep; 0xDD..0xEF from the 2026-04-22T22:30Z third re-sweep (split into two short bursts after a fresh session unlock to avoid the Windows screen-grab failure that killed the earlier attempts).

No second-order mirror: the byte16 values 0xC9..0xEF (which would correspond to 0x65..0x8B if the mirror pattern cycled) all read 'No Device', so the device-selection table is strictly 0x01..0x2A plus its single mirror at 0x65..0x8E, with no further periodicity.

The full 0x00..0xEF byte16 space is now characterised: 42 primary devices (0x01..0x2A), their mirrors (0x65..0x8E), two rejection zones (0x2B..0x64 and 0x8F..0xEF), and sentinel 0x00. No remaining byte16 slots for the 16 still-unmapped canonical devices — EBD-USB+, EBC-A05+, EBC-A20+, EBC-A50L, EBD-M03+, EBD-M05, EBD-M10, EBC-A10+, EBD-A100L, EBC-A40L-40A, EBD-A20H-200W, EBD-B20H-72V3, EBC-B20H-72V3, EBC-B20H-108V3, EBD-B30H-72V3, EBD-B10H-V3. They must therefore be selected by a mechanism other than byte16 alone, most plausibly info-packet bytes 14/15 magic values gating '+' and '-V3' variants on top of a base byte16 that is already in the primary mapping.

One anomaly observed in a prior sweep: (byte14=0xEF, byte15=0xEF, byte16=0x0A) showed EBC-A instead of EBC-A40L. Mechanism unknown — possibly bytes 14/15 override in some edge case. This anomaly is the strongest concrete hint that the 16 unmapped devices use a bytes-14/15 gating path; see PLAN-ui-exploration.md task 1.4.

0x00.note: Probe failed; inferred 'No Device' from context. UI likely displays 'No Device' when byte16=0x00.

0x0a.note: Real hardware reference device — this mapping is cross-validated against the physical EBC-A40L.

0x2b..0x64.note: All 58 values in this range display 'No Device'. Verified directly by OCR of probe screenshots for every byte except 0x35 (probe failed; inferred).

0x65..0x8e.note: Each byte N in this range mirrors byte16 N-0x64 (i.e. 0x65→0x01, 0x6A→0x06, etc.). All captured readings matched the primary range where both probes were clean. See device-names.curated.json for per-byte mirror validations.

0x8f..0xef.note: All 97 values in this range display 'No Device'. OCR row 1 confirmed 'No Device' on every probe. Provenance: 0x8f..0xb8 from the original 2026-04-22 sweep; 0xb9..0xdc from the 2026-04-22T18:00Z re-sweep; 0xdd..0xef from the 2026-04-22T22:30Z third re-sweep (split into two bursts, screenshots at 1.5× DPI merged into the main probe dir via OCR with scaled row regions). Where the raw OCR output shows a device name (EBC-A01 or EBD-A20H) in row 2 for these bytes, that's UI display latching from a prior recognised probe — not a real mapping. See device-names.curated.json note 'rowInterpretation'.

deprecatedKnownTypeCodes._comment: PREVIOUS hypothesis: info-packet bytes 14+15 were the device identifier. This is now known to be wrong — the UI does NOT use these bytes for name lookup (see deviceIdByte above). Kept here for reference; do not use for new code. Bytes 14+15 on the info packet appear to be device-capability fields (likely max current + firmware revision, unverified).
deprecatedKnownTypeCodes.0x11,0x86: EBC-A40L — these are the capability bytes on the real device, NOT its identifier
